references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews describes Abraham's faith when he was tested and offered Isaac, counting on God being able to raise him from the dead.
James writes that Abraham was justified by works when he offered his son Isaac on the altar – a direct reference to the event in Gen 22:9.
God blesses Isaac because Abraham obeyed His voice and kept His commandments – Abraham's obedience in the offering is part of the background.
Typological parallel: Just as Abraham was willing to offer his only son, God did not spare His own Son but gave Him for us all.
God's command to Abraham to go to Moriah and offer Isaac as a burnt offering – the direct occasion for verse 9.
Abraham builds an altar to the Lord during his early stays in Canaan – a pattern of altar-building that culminates in 22:9.
The direct narrative context shows the preparations (wood and journey) that immediately lead to the actual act of offering.
The Letter to the Hebrews gives the theological interpretation of Abraham's action on the altar as a demonstration of faith.
The direct introduction to the test (22:1) is inseparable from its actual execution (22:9).
